title: Defeated, then victorious
hookLine: the Romans have been defeated, and within a few years will win (30:2–4)

lines: A SURAH OPENS WITH A HEADLINE.
cards: News of a far-off war reaches Mecca. Two empires are fighting: the Romans of Constantinople, whom historians now call the Byzantines, and the Persians. The Romans are losing.
In Mecca, far from the fighting, people take sides.

A report in Tirmidhi says the Muslims wanted the Romans to win, since they were people of a scripture, and the Quraysh wanted the Persians, who, like them, had no scripture. Then a surah opens with a headline.

teach.b: Surah Ar-Rum, the Romans, the thirtieth. Pickthall: "The Romans have been defeated". In the nearer land, the verses go on, and after their defeat they will be victorious, within a few years.

teach.h: BID' SININ: A HANDFUL OF YEARS.
teach.b: The phrase is bid' sinin. Bid' means a handful, a small number; the same report in Tirmidhi gives it as between three and nine. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's help.

The report says Abu Bakr was so sure that he made a wager with some of them, before wagers like that were forbidden, and when the Romans won, he won it. Tradition says the emperor Heraclius turned the war.

Some commentators link the believers' rejoicing to the same season as their own victory at Badr; others read it differently, and scholars have discussed exactly which events fit. But the verses don't stay with empires.

teach.h: GOD'S IS THE COMMAND, BEFORE AND AFTER.
teach.b: The next lines say: God's is the command, before and after. Then the surah widens into a long meditation on signs: night and day, rain on dead earth, the cycle of life.
In the surah's picture, a defeat isn't the end of a story. It's a chapter. The defeated can win within a handful of years, and the One who turns it is the One who brings green out of dead ground.

how: Muslims read the opening of Surah Ar-Rum as a prophecy fulfilled in the Byzantine recovery under Heraclius, and as a reminder that the outcome of events belongs to God.

o: the Persians' final fall in a single year
Ar-Rum's opening: the Romans lost, then would win

games.q: you're in Mecca. the Romans have been defeated. the verse says they'll win within a few years. the Quraysh laugh. what does Abu Bakr do?
o: make a wager that it will come true.
games.why: a report in Tirmidhi says he wagered with some of the Quraysh, before such wagers were forbidden, and won.

practice: Think of one place where you're losing right now: your health, a project that keeps failing, a relationship gone cold, a habit that keeps winning.

Don't pretend it isn't a defeat; hold it, then imagine the same scene a handful of years from now, turned around, and notice what small step points that way. If you pray, you can ask for help with it.

wordCard.voice: Defeated. The opening of Ar-Rum: the Romans have been defeated, and after their defeat they will win, within a handful of years. Today's word.
